messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Estonian, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Estonian line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table (Estonian translation)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|----------------------|----------------------|--------| | ove | locative subordinator “where” | **kus** | where | OK | | udirai | future 2nd sg “you will hear” | **kuuled** | you will hear | OK | | le | definite article, fem. pl | *(none)* | – | UNNECESSARY | | disperate | adjective “despairing” (modifies *strida*) | **meeleheite** | of despairing | OK | | strida | plural noun “shrieks” (object of *udirai*) | **karjeid** | shrieks | OK | | vedrai | future 2nd sg “you will see” | **näed** | you will see | OK | | li | definite article, masc. pl | *(none)* | – | UNNECESSARY | | antichi | adjective “ancient/old” (modifies *spiriti*) | **vanu** | ancient | OK | | spiriti | plural noun “spirits” (object of *vedrai*) | **vaime** | spirits | OK | | dolenti | adjective “woeful” (post‑nominal) | **kurbade** | woeful | OK | | ch' | relative pronoun “who” introducing clause | **kes** | who | OK | | a | preposition “to/toward” (governs *seconda morte*) | **poole** | toward | OK | | la | definite article, fem. sg | *(none)* | – | UNNECESSARY | | seconda | ordinal adjective “second” (modifies *morte*) | **teise** | second | OK | | morte | noun “death” (object of *a*) | **surma** | death | OK | | ciascun | distributive quantifier “each” | **igaüks** | each | OK | | grida | verb “shouts/cries out” (3rd sg) | **karjub** | shouts | OK |
### Issues Detected - **UNNECESSARY**: Articles **le**, **li**, **la** have no direct equivalents in Estonian and are omitted. - No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** problems were found; the Estonian rendering respects number, case, and word order required by the target language.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Estonian script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Estonian text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
